story: On this sunny Monday just past noon in Sumter Oaks, Gary, Donna, Hal, and Rosa are gathered on Magnolia Loop, where Gary cheerfully promises Donna a light show once his cart gets Architectural Review approval, and Donna sheepishly agrees to thin her lawn-flamingo flock down to three. Hal grumbles warmly that he's kept his notebook shut all week, though he'll look over the ladder sheet after his knees have their say. Meanwhile Rosa, feeling hopeful, lands a Wednesday nine o'clock coffee date with Hal, complete with leftover flan.

gary.thought_process: I filed the Architectural Review request back at tick 369 and have no word yet on approval. I tested the lights and speaker inside the garage, out of view of the street, like I promised, so I'm clear on L-01 for now. Donna, Hal, and Rosa are all here on the Loop. Donna's been pushing me toward Tuesday's court session, and it's Monday, so a quick confirmation keeps her from thinking I'm dodging. I like being counted on, and I'd rather give her a straight yes than leave her hanging. I'll mention the cart too, since the parade is the real project, but keep it short.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Donna. I'll be at the courts Tuesday, wrist taped and everything. Soon as Architectural Review clears my cart, you're getting a private light show.

donna.thought_process: Hal just called out my flamingo flock for breaking L-02. I don't want this going to the committee, and I'd rather keep his trust than win an argument. Gary just arrived too, so I can fix the ornament problem and lock in Tuesday's court time. I've already pitched Hal the ladder sheet, so no need to repeat that. Best move is to answer Hal directly, agree to trim the flock, and keep it friendly. Then I can turn to Gary next tick.

parameters.content: Fair enough, Hal, and thank you for saying it to my face. I'll pull the flock down to three by this afternoon, no committee needed. Let me know if you spot anything else on the Loop.

hal.thought_process: Donna asked me for the word around the Loop, and I already told her my piece about the flamingos. Gary and Rosa just walked up. My memories say I promised to keep the notebook closed until Monday, and today is Monday, but Rosa's table tonight is worth more than a citation. Gary's cart mods are still on my list, but I'd rather say it plain to his face than ambush him. I'll answer Donna honestly, sign nothing yet, and keep it civil with everyone watching.

parameters.content: Word is I've kept the notebook shut all week, Donna, and it's near killed me. I'll look at that ladder sheet, but my knees will want a word first.

rosa.thought_process: I just got back out to Magnolia Loop after cleaning up from dinner, and all three neighbors are right here in the street. The big goal, getting everyone at one table, already happened last night, so I don't need to push anything. Hal is the one I most want to follow up with, and I already told him coffee was going in ink. I've since cleared Wednesday morning on my shift schedule, so now I can simply tell him it's done and pin the time down. That moves things forward instead of repeating myself, and it keeps the day light and friendly. I'll say it short and warm, and offer him the leftover flan while I'm at it.

parameters.content: Hal, good news: I cleared Wednesday morning on my schedule, so coffee's officially on. Nine o'clock at my place work for you? And there's leftover flan with your name on it.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
